findings.body:
The `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapper was removed when these handlers moved under `/api/v2`. `listUsers` and `editRoles` are now registered as bare `http.HandlerFunc` values on the subrouter, so the admin role gate no longer runs.

**Failure mode:** any authenticated (or unauthenticated, depending on outer middleware) caller can GET `/api/v2/admin/users` and POST `/api/v2/admin/roles` without holding the admin role — privilege escalation / unauthorized admin access.

**Fix:** keep the PathPrefix move, but re-apply the role check on the subrouter or each route:

```suggestion
        v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
        authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")
        v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
        v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

Or `v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))` if that helper returns suitable `mux` middleware.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical authorization regression: the admin role middleware was dropped while relocating the routes under `/api/v2`.

## Analysis

`cmd/server/routes.go` previously wrapped both handlers with `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` before registering `/admin/users` (GET) and `/admin/roles` (POST). The new code creates a `PathPrefix("/api/v2")` subrouter and registers the same handlers as bare `http.HandlerFunc` values — no `Use()`, no per-route wrapper, and no other file in this repo re-applies that check.

Concrete failure mode: any caller who can reach the process can invoke user listing and role editing at `/api/v2/admin/users` and `/api/v2/admin/roles` without an admin role. That is broken authorization on privileged endpoints, not a cosmetic routing cleanup.

Secondary contract note (not filed separately): clients still calling `/admin/users` and `/admin/roles` will 404 after this ships; coordinate the path move with consumers or keep temporary aliases once authz is restored.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Base registered listUsers/editRoles behind middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head moved them under /api/v2 as bare HandlerFuncs with no role check and no other auth middleware in the tree. That is a real critical privilege-escalation regression on the admin endpoints.
